# MAME 68000 core

The files in this folder are MAME's microcode-based 68000 core, copied
unmodified from `src/devices/cpu/m68000/`:

| File                  | Content                                           |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `m68000.h/.cpp`       | The device                                        |
| `m68000-head.h`       | Declarations of the generated microcode handlers  |
| `m68000-decode.cpp`   | Opcode decoding table                             |
| `m68000-sdf.cpp`      | Generated handlers (direct, full)                 |
| `m68000-sdp.cpp`      | Generated handlers (direct, partial)              |
| `m68kcommon.h`        | Shared definitions                                |

* Source: https://github.com/mamedev/mame
* Commit: `d077ea24f0a73118bee9558bc939b99ae662bfc5`
* License: BSD-3-Clause (Olivier Galibert and the MAME team)

The handlers have been generated by MAME from the microcode listing
(`m68000gen.py`, `m68000.lst`). Only the variants for a CPU without an external
MMU are included.

The core is a MAME device. To compile it outside of MAME, a minimal device
framework is provided in `../MAMEGlue/shim/emu.h`. `../MAMEGlue/MameCpu.h` is a
small wrapper that runs the core instruction by instruction and records the bus
cycles. It also allows to trigger a bus error on any access.

To update the core, replace the files and rebuild. `exceptionmame --check` (see
`Tests/Exception`) runs the core against the SingleStepTests, which have been
recorded from the same core. It must report 100%.
